$comment: Audit trail for the LabelVerify routine-test subset. The runtime ID list lives in benchmarks/routine.ts; this file is the human-readable index that explains why each label was picked. If you change one, change the other in the same commit. See docs/MODEL-SELECTION.md §3.5 for the policy on routine vs. full bake-off.
rationale: Hand-curated minimum-overlap subset covering every important axis: beverage type (beer / wine / spirits / fortified-wine), government-warning non-compliance taxonomy (X1 / T1 / C1 / B1 / S2 / X3), degradation classes (perspective / lowlight / occlusion / curved), and historically-tricky cases (stylized all-caps brand, small container). Reproducibility matters more than coverage maximization here — a routine run today must compare apples-to-apples with the same run last week, which is why the set is committed rather than sampled.

labels.reason: Synthetic beer, 200 ml, single-brand archetype, gov_warning_case=null. Baseline pass case for the beer beverage type.
Synthetic wine, 355 ml, single-brand archetype, gov_warning_case=null. Baseline pass case for the wine beverage type.
Synthetic spirits (Fox's Lantern), 355 ml, gov_warning_case=null. Baseline pass case for the distilled-spirits beverage type.
Government warning entirely absent. The hardest-fail case in the taxonomy; routine must catch it.
Warning body contains a paraphrased word ('issues' for 'problems'). Exercises the exact-text regulation check, not just presence detection.
Prefix rendered as 'Government Warning:' instead of 'GOVERNMENT WARNING:'. Exercises the all-caps prefix detector independently of the body text.
Prefix in regular font weight (matches the body). Exercises the bold-prefix detector that pixel-density heuristics alone are weak on.
100 ml container with prefix glyph below the 1 mm minimum. Exercises the size-vs-container-volume rule (§ 16.22).
Foreign-language paraphrase present but the regulated English statement is absent. Routine must not silently pass bilingual fakeouts.
Compliant content (gov_warning_case=null) under 9° perspective skew. Catches preprocessor / homography regressions independently of any warning fault.
Compliant content with lowlight:0.35 illumination drop. Catches CLAHE / tone-curve preprocessor regressions; OCR-only baselines historically degrade fast here.
Compliant content with occlusion:0.12 (12 % of the label face blocked). Routine sanity-check for partial-label robustness.

Curved label surface with a T4 numeral-reorder fault layered on top. Exercises both the dewarp preprocessor and the warning-text exactness check in one cheap label. No purely curved-and-compliant label exists in the corpus today; picking this two-fault case is the highest-value substitute.
All-caps stylized brand (SALTGRASS) on an otherwise compliant label. Catches the failure mode where a brand-name detector trips on the GOVERNMENT WARNING prefix or vice versa.

100 ml wine label that meets the size minimum. Pairs with syn-beer-0017 above to disambiguate true-pass vs. true-fail on small containers — the size rule depends on the container volume, not just the glyph size.
